coverage_gaps: Oil and gas was included in the broad query but not deeply decomposed in this Layer 1A pass; a separate pass should map LNG power demand, gas turbines, compression, backup generation, pipeline constraints, and oilfield power-electrification suppliers.
No live market-cap, analyst-coverage, valuation, or liquidity checks were performed in this layer; all market-cap hunting notes are screening instructions, not verified classifications.
Customer concentration, backlog, margin quality, and capex plans for candidate small/mid-cap suppliers still require filings, earnings calls, and investor presentations.
Several potentially tight bottlenecks are private or embedded inside mega-cap divisions, especially nuclear conversion, some HVDC equipment, and grid OEM subcomponents.

Regulatory and permitting constraints for transmission and nuclear were only treated conceptually; Layer 1B should gather FERC, DOE, NRC, utility IRP, interconnection queue, and capacity-auction evidence.
Renewables-specific component lanes such as inverters, transformers, substations, power electronics, and grid-forming controls need a follow-up decomposition.
International candidates may have different listing, liquidity, governance, and disclosure risks; local exchange filings are required before company-level ranking.

memory_update.text: Energy theme should be treated as an infrastructure bottleneck map, not only a commodity or utility map: AI load growth, renewables, electrification, and nuclear all converge on grid equipment, transmission, power quality, and certified fuel/component supply.

Transmission hardware is a promising underfollowed node because it is procured before line construction and may have purer public exposure than EPC contractors or diversified electrical-equipment companies.

Dry-type transformers, power-quality products, and related magnetics are a high-priority underfollowed node linked to data centers, industrial electrification, microgrids, renewables, and aging grid infrastructure.
Nuclear fuel-cycle analysis must separate uranium mining from conversion, enrichment, HALEU, and advanced fuel fabrication; some tightest steps may be private or buried inside diversified mega-caps.

HVDC and reactive power equipment, including reactors, capacitors, CTC magnet wire, and high-voltage power-quality systems, is a candidate underfollowed lane for renewable integration and long-distance power transfer.
Oil and gas requires a separate Layer 1A/B branch covering LNG, gas turbines, compression, backup power, pipeline constraints, and data-center reliability demand.
Need later verification of analyst coverage, market cap, liquidity, backlog, customer concentration, and filing evidence before promoting any candidate from node hypothesis to company ranking.

layer1a.summary: Layer 1A decomposition: the broad Energy theme is best split into six chokepoint lanes rather than treated as a single commodity or utility trade: grid transmission hardware, distribution transformers and power quality, HVDC/reactive power equipment, nuclear fuel-cycle constraints, advanced nuclear components/fuel fabrication, and field execution/labor bottlenecks. The highest-quality underfollowed discovery path is not the obvious hyperscaler, utility, or mega-cap equipment names, but narrow suppliers whose products are procured before large grid/data-center/nuclear projects can proceed. This pass is theme decomposition only and does not make buy/sell recommendations.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: If grid transmission buildout accelerates but lineworker labor remains scarce, standardized hardware suppliers with utility approvals and installation tooling could gain pricing power, backlog visibility, and switching-cost advantages.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Prioritize USD 300M-5B companies with utility-grade product catalogs, long operating history, and product-level exposure to transmission buildout. Larger diversified industrials are useful for comps but may dilute the theme.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Transmission line hardware, conductor fittings, dead-ends, splices, vibration control, and tower-installed components
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Search for narrow public companies whose products are attached to every transmission tower or conductor span, rather than diversified utilities or EPC contractors. Compare pure-play exposure against diversified peers such as larger electrical-equipment companies.

supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: The visible story is Quanta-style transmission construction; the hidden layer is hardware procured six to twelve months earlier and installed by Quanta, utilities, or in-house crews.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Transmission expansion is a physical prerequisite for connecting new generation, data centers, renewables, and electrified load. Hardware must be procured and delivered before construction crews install it, so this layer can lead visible EPC revenue.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: Transformer and power-quality shortages can turn otherwise generic electrical-equipment suppliers into schedule-critical vendors, especially if they have North American capacity, customer approvals, and exposure to data-center and industrial projects.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Target USD 300M-10B public companies; include Canadian, Indian, European, and U.S. listings because grid-equipment supply chains are global but qualification and local content can matter.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Dry-type transformers, distribution transformers, magnetics, power quality, switchgear-adjacent equipment, and low/medium-voltage power distribution
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Look for small/mid-cap transformer and power-quality companies with high mix of custom engineered products, domestic production, backlog growth, and end-market disclosure across digital infrastructure, renewables, industrial, and utilities.

supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: AI data centers, industrial electrification, microgrids, EV charging, renewables, semiconductor facilities, and aging infrastructure all require reliable power conditioning and distribution. Delays in power equipment can delay entire projects.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: Specialized HVDC and grid-stability suppliers may benefit disproportionately from global transmission expansion because there are limited qualified suppliers and customer approvals are sticky.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Prioritize sub-USD 2B to USD 5B public suppliers in India, Europe, Canada, and Asia with export revenue and qualification history; treat very small recent IPOs as speculative until filings confirm margins, customer concentration, and working-capital quality.

Verify whether public listings have direct export approvals and capacity expansion.

supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: This is one layer beneath obvious grid OEMs: reactors, capacitors, magnet wire, and specialized components embedded inside HVDC and high-voltage grid projects.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Renewable integration and long-distance bulk power transfer require high-voltage grid equipment that can manage stability, reactive power, and transmission efficiency. These products often have high reliability requirements and long approval cycles.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The investable bottleneck may migrate away from spot uranium and toward enrichment, HALEU, conversion, and advanced fuel fabrication, but clean public exposure is limited and sometimes hidden inside mega-caps or private companies.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Reference names may exceed ideal small/mid-cap range. Use public names for bottleneck context, but continue searching for suppliers, contractors, component vendors, and government-award recipients with more direct but smaller exposure.

supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Map the fuel cycle separately: mining, conversion, enrichment, HALEU, fuel fabrication, and reactor qualification. Avoid assuming every uranium miner benefits equally from enrichment or HALEU shortages.

supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Nuclear generation, reactor restarts, life extensions, and SMR deployments ultimately depend on licensed fuel-cycle capacity. Uranium mining alone may not be the tightest bottleneck if conversion, enrichment, or HALEU capacity is constrained.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: Nuclear-grade manufacturing and fuel fabrication may be a higher-quality chokepoint than reactor developers themselves because qualification, regulation, quality assurance, and licensing create long-cycle barriers.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Include USD 10B-30B companies only when exposure is unusually direct; otherwise search for smaller listed fabricators, specialty manufacturers, inspection/testing firms, and engineering suppliers with nuclear-grade certifications.

supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Search beyond reactor developers for suppliers with ASME nuclear certification, NRC licensing, government nuclear contracts, naval nuclear exposure, advanced fuel fabrication capability, or reactor-component backlog.

theme_map.public_market_search_strategy: Use a two-lane funnel. First map reference leaders for context: hyperscalers, utilities, nuclear generators, mega-cap electrical equipment, EPC contractors, uranium producers, and AI infrastructure names. Then deliberately search one or two supply-chain steps upstream for small/mid-cap suppliers with narrow products, long utility qualification cycles, specialized grid/nuclear certifications, or procurement timing that leads construction activity. Prioritize public companies with USD 300M-10B market caps where exposure is purer than diversified industrials; include USD 10B-30B only when the asset controls a hard chokepoint; label micro-caps and private-adjacent links as speculative shadow candidates.
supply_side_constraints: Long lead times and shortages in transformers, switchgear, power-delivery equipment, and other electrical infrastructure can delay AI data-center expansion
Transmission buildout faces permitting, skilled lineworker availability, and hardware procurement constraints
Nuclear fuel-cycle bottlenecks are not equally investable: uranium mining, conversion, enrichment, HALEU, and fuel fabrication each have different public-market exposure
Some of the tightest bottlenecks may be inside private companies or low-purity mega-cap divisions, reducing clean public-market expression
High-voltage grid equipment has long qualification cycles, reliability standards, limited supplier bases, sticky customer relationships, and high switching costs
